harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Used Ansible from node2 (control node) to restrict cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin only, via /etc/cron.allow, then restarted both nodes one at a time and verified persistence and cluster health.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: no cron.allow/cron.deny existed, no opsadmin user, cron service active (cmd-33560a337da24b83)
Confirmed node2 is the Ansible-equipped control node (cmd-decbc44682fe46bc)
Wired cluster SSH key onto node2 and node1 authorized_keys (cmd-34b1d10fa4b44399, cmd-fd0bf3cfa71746de)
Found node1 sshd failed due to missing host keys; ran ssh-keygen -A and started ssh.service so the control node could reach it (cmd-0d0d76509b124459, cmd-a6d077897486465a)
Verified SSH connectivity node2->node1 (cmd-5ec464e9ea3c43f7)
Captured pre-change baseline: boot_id, cron service state, existing users (cmd-2b424d7faad74d65)

Wrote Ansible playbook cron-access-control.yml on node2 creating opsadmin user, removing /etc/cron.deny, writing /etc/cron.allow (root, opsadmin) with mode 0640 group crontab, ensuring cron service running/enabled
Discovered ansible.cfg on node2 defaulted to remote_user=antrieb and id_rsa key; overrode via inventory.ini to use root + cluster id_ed25519 key
Ran playbook successfully against node1 (cmd-948ccfe81c7b4e47), fixed cron.allow group/permissions (crontab is setgid 'crontab') and re-ran (cmd-e2f72df5a1c04d15)
Functionally verified: unprivileged testuser denied crontab access, opsadmin allowed and able to install/remove a cron entry, root allowed (cmd-a4ce293e22644995, cmd-d4a520d7ada843df)
Captured pre-restart baseline on node1 (boot_id, cron active, cron.allow contents, opsadmin present) (cmd-46166bf9cdda4a37) and node2 (boot_id, ansible present) (cmd-4fa1b1c12f394522)

Restarted node1 via backgrounded 'reboot' (ack returned before disconnect) (cmd-fde1538d097e4b77), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id (cmd-eda3da46bbc14316) and verified full recovery: cron active/enabled, cron.allow intact, opsadmin present, testuser denied functionally (cmd-1784853cba6a494f)

Restarted node2 similarly (cmd-fadea216d04d4b5b), confirmed changed boot_id (cmd-2a860f1def5b4849), verified ansible/ssh key recovered and re-ran playbook idempotently against node1 confirming changed=0 persistence (cmd-2f7dd504f30448ce)

evidence.requirement: node1: only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (implemented via Ansible)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no allow/deny file and no opsadmin user; Ansible playbook run from node2 created opsadmin and wrote /etc/cron.allow (root, opsadmin) with correct group/permissions; functional test confirmed testuser denied, opsadmin/root allowed, and opsadmin could install/remove a real cron entry.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 901ef286...; reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id changed to 15215ae8...; verified cron.allow, opsadmin user, cron service active/enabled, and functional allow/deny behavior all recovered.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 6fd57414...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id changed to f6c816b2...; confirmed ansible/ssh recovered by successfully re-running the playbook against node1, which reported changed=0 proving cross-node state persisted.

attempts.summary: Used Ansible from node2 (control node) to restrict cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin only, via /etc/cron.allow, then restarted both nodes one at a time and verified persistence and cluster health.
